Latvian parliament gives “green light” to possible state involvement in airBaltic rescue
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
09:58:34 UTC
18:58:34 KST

The Latvian parliament on Thursday gave its preliminary approval to possible state participation in the financial stabilisation of national airline airBaltic, including the potential purchase of up to thirty million euros in bridge-financing bonds and the conversion of fifty million euros in existing bonds into equity.
The bill has been designated as urgent.
The legislation would authorise the government to potentially participate in the purchase of up to thirty million euros in airBaltic bridge-financing bonds alongside private investors and on identical terms. The Cabinet of Ministers would be able to make a separate decision on purchasing the bonds if necessary.
The plan also provides for converting claims arising from a state loan and bonds already held by the state into the airline’s share capital. This means that fifty million euros in state-owned bonds and more than eighteen million euros remaining under the state loan could be converted into airBaltic shares.
The repayment deadline for the thirty-million-euro state loan is also expected to be extended from the end of August until the end of this year. By July 24, airBaltic had repaid a total of 12.9 million euros in principal and contractual interest payments on the state loan.
This week, airBaltic bondholders approved the capitalisation of the next two bond interest payments, as well as several other measures giving the airline additional flexibility in implementing its revised business plan.
Bondholders approved adding the interest payments due on August 14 and November 14 this year to the principal amount of the bonds instead of paying them in cash. They also approved a temporary waiver of minimum liquidity requirements until November 2026.
Meanwhile, airBaltic’s planned raising of 225 million euros in bridge financing was not considered at the bondholders’ meeting on Monday, August 17, because the issue was not included on the agenda.
The purpose of the bill is to establish measures for airBaltic’s financial stabilisation and ensure effective management of the state’s financial interests during the process. It would allow the state, as a shareholder, creditor and bondholder, to act in a timely and coordinated manner and on an equal footing with the airline’s other shareholders, bondholders and creditors.
One or more of the measures set out in the bill could be implemented to stabilise airBaltic’s finances. Decisions on individual measures would be taken by the Cabinet of Ministers, which would determine their scope, implementation conditions and other relevant terms.
Among the measures envisaged is an amendment to the agreement covering the thirty-million-euro state loan to the airline, extending the deadline for repayment of the outstanding principal, accrued interest and other obligations arising from the agreement.
The bill also provides for the full or partial conversion into equity of any claims arising from the thirty-million-euro state loan granted to airBaltic.
Another possible measure would allow claims arising from airBaltic bonds held by the state to be capitalised, converted or otherwise restructured up to the actual outstanding principal amount of those bonds, but not exceeding fifty million euros, plus the relevant accrued interest and other claims arising from the bonds.
The bill also states that the state could participate in providing bridge financing to airBaltic by purchasing up to thirty million euros in newly issued airBaltic bonds.
The newly issued bonds would be purchased in accordance with the bond issue documentation, including the prospectus and instructions from the issue arrangers. The Ministry of Transport would be responsible for preparing financial, legal, fiscal and state-aid assessments, as well as the terms of the bridge-financing transaction.
The Cabinet of Ministers would be required to report to the Saeima Budget and Finance Committee on the implementation of the financial stabilisation measures at least once every quarter.
As previously reported, airBaltic’s Supervisory Board has approved a business plan that includes raising 225 million euros in interim financing to improve liquidity, using the existing collateral package securing its 2029 senior bonds.
In the longer term, the plan envisages recapitalising the company through up to 225 million euros in new debt and 100 million euros in new equity. Part of the existing 2029 bonds would be converted into shares in the company, while the remainder would be replaced with new, smaller debt of up to 125 million euros.
The business plan also envisages airBaltic operating 36 Airbus A220-300 aircraft by the end of 2026, compared with 54 aircraft currently, with the fleet gradually increasing to around 40 aircraft by 2031.
The airBaltic Group generated revenue of 779.344 million euros last year, an increase of 4.2% compared with 2024. The group posted a loss of 44.337 million euros, which was 2.7 times lower than in 2024. In 2025, the airline carried a total of 5.2 million passengers, an increase of 1% compared with 2024.
German flag carrier Lufthansa became an airBaltic shareholder last summer. The Latvian state currently owns 88.37% of airBaltic, Lufthansa holds 10%, Danish businessman Lars Thuesen’s Aircraft Leasing 1 owns 1.62%, and other shareholders hold the remaining 0.01%. The company’s share capital stands at 41.819 million euros.
In light of its 2025 financial results and current market conditions, airBaltic has suspended its potential initial public offering and does not currently consider an IPO a potential source of capital in 2026, according to the airline’s annual report.

Nearly 40,000 take shelter in Kyiv metro stations overnight
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
12:54:28 EEST
18:54:28 KST

Over 38,000 people, including more than 2,000 children, took shelter in Kyiv metro stations on the night leading into August 20, the press service of Kyiv City State Administration reported, citing Kyiv Metro utility company.
"On the night leading into August 20, during another massive shelling of the capital, over 38,000 people, including more than 2,000 children, were at Kyiv metro stations. Last night, the air raid alert lasted nearly 9 hours," Kyiv Metro reported, according to the administration’s website.
It is noted that 46 underground stations of the Kyiv metro operate around the clock as shelters during air raid alerts. All lobbies are opened for entry to make the route to safety as short as possible. Metro employees, together with police, ensure prompt and unhindered access to the stations.
The enterprise reminds that if there is a need to use the metro as a shelter in advance, people should arrive at the station before it finishes passenger transport operations. Operating schedules are posted at every station. Where possible, it is recommended to choose central stations, which typically offer more space to accommodate people.
Visitors are requested to bring only essential items and avoid using bulky items, particularly mattresses and tents. These occupy a significant portion of space needed by others during enemy shelling.
The enterprise also emphasizes the need to avoid sitting on escalators or leaving belongings on them. In the event of an emergency or the need for urgent evacuation, escalators must be brought into operation quickly. The presence of people or oversized items on them can slow down this process.
As reported, during the overnight attack on July 30, over 56,000 people took shelter in the metro system, and on July 2, 52,500 residents used it, including nearly 4,500 children.

Gangs suspected of stealing fire station equipment for ram-raids
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
09:53:24 UTC
18:53:24 KST

Gangs suspected of stealing fire station equipment for ram-raids
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
More than 60 fire stations have been targeted in the last year by criminal gangs who steal hydraulic equipment to use in ram raids.
One fire station in Sassenheim, near Leiden in Zuid-Holland, was attacked three nights in a row in the last week, while 10 sites have been broken into across the country in the last fortnight.
Police told NRC the thieves were looking for equipment such as cutting gear and hydraulic jacks used to free people who are trapped beneath rubble.
The machines can be repurposed to break heavily fortified windows used by shops such as jewellers and electrical retailers. Last week thieves left behind a hydraulic spreader that they used to try to smash the window of a jewellery store in Den Bosch.
The number of break-ins has jumped in the last year, with just 18 thefts from fire stations recorded in 2025 and 17 the year before.
“We are trying to strengthen our response teams and making detecting these crimes a national priority,” police spokesman Dick Goijert said.
Safety boards would not say exactly what was taken in the most recent raids because the police investigation is ongoing and to avoid giving “unnecessary information to people with bad intentions”.
Accessibility issues
Fire station managers have tried to improve security, but locking away life-saving equipment means it takes longer to retrieve it in an emergency, when a few lost seconds can make the difference between life and death.
Evert Jansen, a former burglar who now works for the police to raise companies’ awareness of the need to improve security, said he suspected organised criminals were behind the thefts.
“Unless they know how the equipment works it’s difficult for them to use it,” Jansen told NRC. “Maybe the burglars are stealing it on the orders of experienced criminals.”

'RSS believes it knows the truth for everyone': Rahul Gandhi attacks Sangh over ideology

2026-08-20

'RSS believes it knows the truth for everyone': Rahul Gandhi attacks Sangh over ideology
Edited by: Rajeev Singh / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 20, 2026, 15:44 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
Rahul Gandhi drew a distinction between the RSS's worldview and Mahatma Gandhi's idea of 'Swaraj.
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi Thursday accused the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of trying to impose its idea of truth on people across India, arguing that every individual must have the freedom to find and define their own truth.Speaking at the "Hara Bhara Swaraj: A Tribute to Rajiv Gandhi's Vision" programme in New Delhi, the Gandhi Scion described the ideological contest in India as a deeper struggle over how people understand themselves, freedom and their place in society.
The Congress leader also drew a distinction between the RSS's worldview and Mahatma Gandhi's idea of 'Swaraj', saying no organisation or individual could claim to know what is true for another person."What Gandhiji was saying was that every living being is a unique entity with their own path towards the truth. I cannot tell you what your truth is. Today, the ideological battle in India is precisely that. It is not fundamentally about environment, politics, or free media--those are symptoms. The real fight is that a small group of people have decided, because they control the system, that they know the truth of everyone in this country.
That is my problem with the RSS: the RSS has decided that they know the truth of 1.5 billion people. And I say, no. Only 1.5 billion people can know their own truth," Rahul Gandhi asserted.He said even he could not claim to understand another person's truth because people's experiences, families and circumstances are different."And I say, no. Only 1.5 billion people can know their own truth. Even I cannot do that. If I begin to believe that I know your truth, I would be a madman. Because I am not you. I haven't faced what you've faced; I haven't seen what you've seen; I haven't dealt with what you've dealt with. I don't have the same parents, the same friends, or the same life. So how can I say that I know your truth?" he added.
‘My Experiments with Truth’ reflects individual journeys
Rahul Gandhi then referred to Mahatma Gandhi's autobiography, 'My Experiments with Truth', saying its title itself reflected the idea that truth is something each person explores through their own life."Please notice, Gandhiji's book was not called 'The Truth' or 'My Understanding of the Truth'. It was titled 'My Experiments with Truth'. I have experiments with my truth; you have experiments with your truth."
Rahul targets BJP-RSS over 'exclusion'
The Congress leader also criticised the BJP and RSS over what he described as the exclusion of sections of Indian society. He said people from different religious and social communities must feel that they have an equal place in the country."Imagine what the BJP and RSS have done. Imagine if I walked into this room and told 15-17 per cent of you--Muslims, Christians, Sikhs--'You do not exist, and if you speak up, see what happens to you.' Then telling 10 per cent Adivasis, 'We will take your land whenever we want, and if you resist, we will shoot you,' and Dalits, 'You are complaining for nothing; everything is fine with the caste system.' That is what is being done to our motherland. Every single person in this country--regardless of religion, community, or gender--must feel: 'I belong here. I can walk freely in this country. I am loved, respected, and appreciated here, and my search for truth matters to the nation,'" he said.
'Gandhi’s Swaraj is more than freedom'
Rahul Gandhi also explained why he believes 'Swaraj' should not simply be understood as the same thing as freedom or liberty in the Western sense.He used US President Donald Trump and Mahatma Gandhi to illustrate the difference, arguing that being legally free does not necessarily mean having control over one's own actions and desires."'Swaraj' is often confused with the Western word 'freedom.' People think that Swaraj means freedom; that it means liberty or independence. No--Swaraj means rule over oneself (Swa par raj / self-governance). If you go to America and ask, 'Is Trump a free man?', everyone will say, 'Absolutely.' But if you ask, 'Does Trump rule over himself?', the clear answer is, 'No, he does not.' Whereas Gandhiji in a prison 80 years ago would say, 'I am not free, but I rule over myself. It is Swaraj,'" he explained.The Congress leader said this understanding of Swaraj makes it a personal responsibility rather than something that can simply be granted by a government or another person."Swaraj is an Indian concept, and it carries deep responsibility. It is a way of thinking, and it is an individual project. I cannot give you Swaraj. Whatever I do... in a Western sense, I can grant you freedom by saying, 'You are not in prison; I have given you freedom.'
But I cannot give you Swaraj. Because Swaraj is your personal relationship with the universe. Swaraj is an individual path. And Gandhiji's conception of Swaraj was that every single person in this country should walk on this path."His remarks placed the idea of individual self-rule at the centre of his criticism of the RSS, while presenting Gandhi's philosophy of Swaraj as one based on personal responsibility and the freedom of each individual to pursue their own understanding of truth.
Rajeev Singh is a Digital Content Producer with The Times of India. He covers politics, policies, defence, and conflicts for readers curious to know their implications. He loves digging into legal maxims and political trivia. On off days, when not turning pages or learning русский, he lives in the reverie of “what ifs” and “how abouts.”

Taiwan to roll out NT$3.33 billion tourism subsidies in September
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
09:51:34 UTC
18:51:34 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Tourism Administration will launch an NT$3.33 billion (US$104 million) tourism promotion package Sept. 1, featuring accommodation subsidies, birthday vouchers, and incentives aimed at attracting both domestic and international travelers.
The domestic program includes five categories: weekday accommodation discounts, birthday accommodation vouchers, amusement park stay incentives, corporate employee travel incentives, and Taiwan PASS discounts, per UDN.
The international component includes four measures, including rewards for repeat visitors, support for MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, and exhibitions) travel, additional incentives for group tours, and support for international flagship concerts.
Domestic travel incentives
Online registration for weekday accommodation and birthday vouchers begins Thursday, according to the Tourism Administration. The weekday accommodation program runs from Sept. 1 to Nov. 30. Weekdays are defined as Sunday through Thursday, excluding national holidays and consecutive holidays.
Travelers staying at participating legal accommodations can receive subsidies for up to two consecutive nights. In general areas, the maximum subsidy is NT$800 for the first night and NT$1,200 for the second night. On outlying islands, the maximum subsidy is NT$1,000 for the first night and NT$1,500 for the second night. The two nights may be spent at different accommodations or in different areas, but the stays must be on consecutive dates.
Completing the online registration only records an applicant's information and does not guarantee a subsidy. Travelers must present either their national identification card or National Health Insurance card at check-in so accommodation operators can verify their identity, per UDN.
The birthday voucher program runs from Sept. 10 to Dec. 31. Each month, 1,000 people celebrating their birthdays will be randomly selected to receive NT$1,200 in accommodation credit. Birthday vouchers can be combined with weekday accommodation subsidies.
The amusement park overnight stay program runs from Sept. 1 to Nov. 30. After registering, customers will receive amusement park points based on the amount of their accommodation discount. The points can be exchanged for admission tickets and related merchandise.
The Taiwan PASS double-savings program runs from Sept. 1 to Dec. 31. Travelers purchasing the Taiwan PASS Taiwan Railway Edition for NT$2,500 can choose between a 50% discount on the pass, saving NT$1,250, or an NT$1,500 weekday accommodation voucher. The accommodation voucher can be combined with weekday accommodation and birthday vouchers.
The corporate employee domestic travel incentive program runs from Sept. 1 to Dec. 15. Companies organizing two-day, one-night employee trips can receive NT$20,000 per group, with a maximum application limit of NT$60,000.
Incentives for international visitors
A special program designed to attract repeat international visitors will run from Oct. 10 through March 31, 2027. It applies to foreign travelers who have previously entered Taiwan since Jan. 1, 2023.
Individual repeat visitors will have a chance to receive NT$5,000 in prepaid credit. Those traveling with companions can receive up to NT$8,000, consisting of NT$5,000 for the repeat visitor and NT$3,000 for accompanying family members or friends.
For international group tours, groups of at least four people in which repeat visitors account for at least 10% of participants will be eligible for subsidies ranging from NT$10,000 to NT$30,000 per group, per UDN.
The program also targets overseas companies organizing incentive trips to Taiwan. In addition to existing subsidies, an additional NT$1,000 per person per night will be provided when travelers stay at legal accommodations south of Taichung, in Hualien or Taitung, or on outlying islands.
The additional subsidy is capped at NT$4,000 per trip. Applications must generally be submitted at least 15 days before arrival, or earlier when the application date falls before a national holiday. The incentive program for international travelers attending conferences and exhibitions in Taiwan will run from Sept. 1 through March 31, 2027.
Eligible visitors can receive a free half-day or full-day Taiwan sightseeing bus tour and a Taiwan PASS High-Speed Rail Edition. The Tourism Administration encouraged travelers to plan ahead and check participating accommodations, booking platforms, and available discounts before making reservations. A list of participating accommodations and booking platforms is available at TaiwanStay.
The Tourism Administration said each national ID number can be used only once in the weekday accommodation and birthday voucher programs. Only one incentive from each program can be used per room per night. For example, if two eligible travelers share a room, only one weekday accommodation subsidy and one birthday voucher can be redeemed for that room on a given night.
Consumers who believe a business has inflated room rates can submit evidence to their local municipal or county government. If the allegations are confirmed, the business may be removed from the program and lose its eligibility to participate.

Türkiye’s population soars to 86.3 mln, official data says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
09:49:33 UTC
18:49:33 KST

Türkiye’s steady mid-year headcount bump has officially pushed the national tally to 86.3 million as of July 1, according to fresh figures released by the Turkish Statistical Institute (TÜİK).
The country’s population, which stood at 86 million at the end of 2025, increased by 228,434 during the first six months of this year, TÜİK said on Aug. 20.
Between May 1 and July 1 alone, the population rose by 123,904.
As of July 1, men accounted for 50.01 percent of the population, while women accounted for 49.99 percent.
By presidential decree, the 2026–2035 period has been designated as the “Decade of Family and Population” in Türkiye.
Led by the Family and Social Services Ministry, the initiative relies on strategic action plans to tackle dwindling birth rates, strengthen family structures and protect the country’s demographic balance.
Drawing on data from TÜİK and other public agencies, a new analytics platform will track family and population trends to help policymakers trace the roots and long-term impacts of demographic shifts.
The strategy comes as Türkiye’s birth rate continues to decline. According to TÜİK, 895,374 babies were born in 2025, with boys accounting for 51.4 percent of births and girls 48.6 percent.
The country’s total fertility rate — the average number of children a woman is expected to have during her lifetime — fell to 1.42 in 2025, down from 2.38 in 2001. It has remained below 2.1 children per woman, the level needed for a population to replace itself without migration, for the past nine years.
The number of provinces with very low birth rates has also increased dramatically. In 2017, only four of the country’s 81 provinces had fertility rates below 1.50, compared with 59 provinces in 2025.

China calls for unity, cooperation among Security Council members
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
17:49:00 CST
18:49:00 KST

UNITED NATIONS, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Unity and cooperation should remain at the core of the Security Council's working methods, a Chinese envoy said on Wednesday.
As the core of the global collective security mechanism, the Security Council's ability to effectively discharge its duties bears on the authority and credibility of the United Nations and the prospects for international peace and security. Its working methods, as an important safeguard for the council in fulfilling its mandate, are by no means merely a technical matter. They should be continuously improved and refined from the broader perspective of maintaining international peace and security, said Fu Cong, China's permanent representative to the United Nations.
"Unity and cooperation are the source of vitality for multilateral mechanisms and should always remain at the core of the Security Council's working methods," he told a Security Council open debate on the council's working methods. "Whether on substantive issues or procedural matters, council members should respect one another, engage in full consultation, properly manage differences, and make every effort to seek consensus."
Rushing draft resolutions to a vote when substantial differences remain among council members not only exacerbates divisions, but also undermines the political weight and effectiveness of resolutions, he said.
The effectiveness of council meetings, outcomes, and tools such as sanctions and peacekeeping should be measured by whether they are grounded in reality and can constructively advance the political settlement of hot-spot issues, said Fu.
He called on council members to seek peaceful solutions to disputes, fully respect the sovereignty and ownership of the countries concerned, and exercise caution in using coercive measures, such as sanctions and force.
"Sanctions regimes that fail to achieve their intended objectives should be promptly reviewed and adjusted, and those that have become obsolete should be lifted in a timely manner," he said.
The Security Council should adjust its deliberation cycles in a timely manner in light of changing circumstances, make appropriate arrangements for discussions on broad thematic issues, and minimize meetings with overlapping content to the greatest extent possible, said Fu. "We should make flexible use of different meeting formats, appropriately increase informal consultations, and promote candid and efficient communication among Council members. We should improve our drafting style and make outcome documents more concise and clear."
The Security Council bears the primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security, and its status and role are irreplaceable, he said, adding that a united and strong Security Council serves the needs of world peace and stability and meets the common interests of the broader UN membership.
"We call on all countries to actively support the work of the Security Council, faithfully implement its resolutions, and jointly uphold its authority. We should oppose illegal unilateral actions that circumvent the Security Council and undermine the authority of the United Nations. Permanent members should play a leading role in this regard, uphold fairness and justice, and truly demonstrate the responsibility of major powers," said Fu.
As a permanent member of the Security Council and a responsible major country, China has always participated constructively in the work of the council. China stands ready to continue working with all parties to uphold multilateralism, strengthen unity and cooperation, and jointly support the council in improving its working methods and enhancing its capacity to fulfill its mandate, so as to play a greater role in building a world of lasting peace and common security, he said. ■

WUHAN, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- A senior Chinese mainland official said on Thursday that the mainland will firmly promote the peaceful development of relations across the Taiwan Strait and integrated cross-Strait development.
Peng Qing'en, deputy head of the Taiwan Work Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council, made the remarks at the opening of a two-day symposium on cross-Strait relations in Wuhan, capital city of central China's Hubei Province.
Peng called on people across the Strait to work together to firmly oppose "Taiwan independence" separatism and external interference, safeguard the shared homeland of the Chinese nation, and work together toward national reunification and national rejuvenation.

People on both sides should expand exchanges and cooperation in all fields and safeguard peace and stability across the Strait, they added.
The Taiwan question is a scar left by a full-blown civil war fought between forces led by the CPC and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC.
This unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has left the two sides of the Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. ■

BEIJING, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese customs anti-smuggling authorities and Australian border enforcement agencies have cracked a major transnational tobacco smuggling case through a joint law enforcement operation, China's Ministry of Public Security said on Thursday.
The two sides seized more than 90 million smuggled cigarettes in the operation, marking a significant outcome in their joint crackdown on transnational tobacco smuggling, the ministry noted.
The case was uncovered during a targeted campaign launched by Zhanjiang Customs anti-smuggling authorities in south China's Guangdong Province to crack down on tobacco smuggling and counterfeit tobacco products.
The authorities unveiled a smuggling network that concealed counterfeit tobacco products made overseas in legitimate cargo for transit via China and onward shipment to Australia.
Chinese authorities shared the relevant leads with Australian border enforcement agencies through an existing customs law enforcement cooperation mechanism, leading to coordinated action by the two sides.
Australian border enforcement authorities praised the operation, saying it demonstrated the importance of international law enforcement cooperation and information sharing in combating transnational tobacco smuggling.
China's customs anti-smuggling authorities said the operation had disrupted channels used to smuggle tobacco into and through China and pledged to step up international cooperation against transnational smuggling. ■

F1: Verstappen extends Red Bull contract to 2030

Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
17:48:38 CST
18:48:38 KST

BEIJING, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Four-time Formula 1 world champion Max Verstappen has signed a contract extension with Red Bull that will keep him with the team through the end of 2030, ending months of speculation over his future.
The 28-year-old Dutchman had been contracted through 2028, but performance-related clauses could have allowed him to leave earlier. He had been linked with possible moves to Mercedes and McLaren as Red Bull struggled at the start of Formula 1's new technical era.
"I am really pleased with the contract extension," Verstappen said. "We have the best people and I'm excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again."
Verstappen described Red Bull as a "second family" and said he remained committed to returning the team to championship contention.
"I came to the team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely and we have shared many incredible moments and won four World Championships," he said.
The announcement comes ahead of this weekend's Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, which is scheduled to drop off the F1 calendar after this year.
Verstappen narrowly missed out on a fifth consecutive drivers' title last season, finishing two points behind McLaren's Lando Norris after recovering from a deficit of more than 100 points during the second half of the year.
Red Bull has found the going tougher since new car and engine regulations were introduced this season. Verstappen's best results have been second-place finishes in Austria and Hungary, and he has voiced frustration with the team's performance.
His decision to stay also comes during a period of significant change at Red Bull. Adrian Newey, longtime motorsport adviser Helmut Marko and former team principal Christian Horner have all left in recent years, while Verstappen's race engineer Gianpiero Lambiase has agreed to join McLaren no later than 2028.
Laurent Mekies replaced Horner as team principal in July 2025, and Verstappen said the Frenchman's leadership had helped convince him about Red Bull's direction.
"Getting to work with Laurent now for over a year has also been great. I see a clear vision he has for the team," Verstappen said. "Everyone in Milton Keynes believes in what we are building and I am looking forward to the next chapter, fighting for more victories and competing for championships."
Mekies called retaining Verstappen "fantastic news" and said the partnership had become one of the most successful in Formula 1 history.
"His impact on our team and on Red Bull's motorsport story has been transformational, and he has been fundamental to everything we have accomplished together," Mekies said.
Although the new agreement runs through 2030, it is understood to contain mechanisms that could allow Verstappen to leave if Red Bull's performance falls below specified levels. Such clauses are common in Formula 1 contracts, although their details are generally kept confidential.
Verstappen made his Formula 1 debut with Red Bull's junior team, then known as Toro Rosso, in 2015. He was promoted to Red Bull after four races of the 2016 season and won on his team debut at the Spanish Grand Prix.
He has since won four world championships and 71 grands prix, placing him third on Formula 1's all-time wins list behind Lewis Hamilton and Michael Schumacher. ■

China Focus: Volkswagen flourishing in east China EV innovation venture
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
17:48:38 CST
18:48:38 KST

HEFEI, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Volkswagen Anhui's 100,000th intelligent electric vehicle (EV) rolled off the production line on Tuesday in Hefei, capital of east China's Anhui Province, marking another milestone in the German automaker's electrification push in China.
Volkswagen Anhui is Volkswagen Group's first joint venture in China that focuses on both the research and development (R&D) and manufacturing of new energy vehicles (NEVs).
"The 100,000th vehicle is far more than a number," said Miroslav Khula, CEO of Volkswagen Anhui. "We will continue to unlock the synergies between German engineering and local innovation, delivering higher-quality products to our customers."
Competition in China's NEV market has evolved beyond product specs and pricing into a multi-dimensional battlefield that spans software, intelligent driving, electronic and electrical architecture, and even supply chain coordination.
The landmark 100,000th EV is an ID. UNYX 08, the first model co-developed by Volkswagen and its Chinese partner XPENG. It went into mass production at Volkswagen Anhui's Hefei plant in March, equipped with localized cutting-edge technologies including 800-volt ultra-fast charging and enhanced L2-level assisted driving.
Volkswagen Group has invested more than 3.5 billion euros in Hefei, where its Volkswagen Group China Technology Company (VCTC), the group's largest R&D center outside Germany, is located, housing about 3,000 R&D professionals.
The zonal electronic and electrical architecture co-developed by VCTC, CARIAD China and XPENG, known as China Electronic Architecture, was delivered at the end of 2025, taking just 18 months from concept to production, the fastest development timeline Volkswagen Group has ever achieved for a brand-new electronic and electrical architecture.
This marks a shift in which global automakers are no longer just manufacturing in China -- they are now integrating their Chinese partners' technological capabilities into their core R&D systems.
Hefei, where Volkswagen Anhui is based, is a key hub in China's NEV industry. In 2025, the city produced over 1.37 million NEVs, the most among all Chinese cities. It is home to major carmakers including JAC, BYD and NIO, along with a supply chain spanning power batteries, automotive electronics and intelligent driving, serving as a nexus between China's market and Volkswagen's global operations.
The all-electric CUPRA Tavascan is Volkswagen Anhui's flagship model for export to Europe, with the Hefei plant the sole global production site. In February, the European Commission accepted Volkswagen Anhui's price undertaking, allowing the CUPRA Tavascan to enter the European market exempt from countervailing duties of up to 20.7 percent.
Volkswagen Anhui's experience is not an isolated case. General Motors recently extended its joint venture with Chinese partner SAIC Motor by 20 years, following a similar move by Honda Motor and China's GAC Group, which renewed their partnership through 2038.
These back-to-back extensions reflect global automakers' confidence in the long-term value of the Chinese market, and, more significantly, their recognition that China's R&D, manufacturing and supply chain capabilities are poised to support their global operations.
According to Khula, under its dual-engine strategy of growing its China business and expanding overseas export, Volkswagen Anhui is strengthening its all-electric ID. UNYX lineup and accelerating the series production and delivery of next-generation intelligent connected vehicles in China, while drawing on the strengths of China's NEV supply chain and intelligent manufacturing ecosystem, particularly in Hefei, to support the group's global production layout.
China's NEV production and sales reached more than 7.43 million and 7.44 million units, respectively, in the first half of 2026, up 6.7 percent and 7.3 percent year on year, according to the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers. NEV exports, meanwhile, surged to over 2.35 million units in this period, a 120-percent increase from a year earlier.
Volkswagen Group plans to speed up its China push in 2026, with more than 20 NEV models across its brands set to hit the market in quick succession, the company added. ■

Dengue cases spread across Nepal as it marks World Mosquito Day
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
17:48:19 CST
18:48:19 KST

KATHMANDU, Aug. 20 (Xinhua) -- Dengue cases have spread across Nepal, with health authorities warning that infections could rise further during and after the monsoon season as the country marks World Mosquito Day on Thursday.
According to the latest analysis by the Epidemiology and Disease Control Division (EDCD) under the Department of Health Services, Nepal reported 2,844 dengue cases in 74 of its 77 districts between Jan. 1 and Aug. 15, meaning infections have now been reported in almost all districts.
Gandaki Province in western Nepal has recorded the highest number of dengue cases with 1,010, followed by Koshi with 674, Lumbini with 435 and Bagmati with 427. Sudurpaschim has reported 122 cases, while Madhesh and Karnali have recorded 88 cases each. Authorities have verified two dengue-related deaths so far in 2026.
The EDCD has been conducting fortnightly assessments of the dengue situation and issuing prevention and control recommendations in areas reporting higher numbers of infections.
It has also launched a three-month dengue awareness campaign running from mid-July to mid-October, focusing on the regular monitoring and elimination of mosquito breeding sites.
The campaign coincides with the global observance of World Mosquito Day on Aug. 20, which is being marked this year in Nepal under the theme "Small Bite, Big Challenge."
The observance comes as mosquito-borne diseases continue to pose a growing public health challenge in Nepal. While more than 3,500 mosquito species have been reported worldwide, 168 species have so far been identified in Nepal, according to the EDCD.
Health authorities have urged the public to remain vigilant during the monsoon and post-monsoon periods, when conditions can favor mosquito breeding. Eliminating stagnant water, regularly cleaning water containers and surrounding areas, and taking measures to prevent mosquito bites are among the key preventive steps being promoted through the campaign. ■

A children’s hospital was struck in the Solomianskyi district to the west of the heart of the capital, with windows blown out and cars burned. At least two residential buildings were also reported hit in the area.
Explosions could be heard from the city centre at about midnight on Wednesday, earlier than the normal timing of Russian missile strikes, and there was a further wave of attacks early on Thursday morning.

Russia-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant loses external power supply
The United Nations nuclear watchdog said on Thursday that Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power station lost its only remaining external power line, forcing emergency diesel generators to start supplying vital safety systems, Reuters reported.
The International Atomic Energy Agency, or IAEA, said on X that initial assessment indicated the damage was located on the northern bank of the Dnipro River, and technicians were unable to determine the outage’s cause due to military activity.
The plant, Europe’s largest with six reactors, produces no electricity but needs power supplied by two external links to keep nuclear fuel cool, Reuters said.
Ukraine’s air force said that Russia had launched dozens of ballistic, cruise, and hypersonic missiles, as well as 168 drones in its overnight attack on the country.
It said that air defence units downed 145 drones and most of the cruise missiles but none of the missiles that run on ballistic trajectory, Reuters said.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has for month been pushing for more anti-ballistic missiles to be delivered to Ukraine.
18 people hospitalised after overnight attacks on Kyiv
Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko said 18 people have been hospitalised after the overnight attacks, with emergency and clean-up response continuing at various sites across three districts of the city.
“The capital is recovering from a massive enemy attack,” he said in a video on Telegram.
“Residential and non-residential buildings, a school, and a children’s hospital were damaged,” he added.
At least 12 people were killed and 40 injured in a series of Russian attacks on the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv.
“It was a massive attack – the Russians had been preparing for a long time, combining different types of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones, aiming to cause as much damage as possible to civilian infrastructure. There is destruction in Kyiv and the region, as well as in the Odesa and Chernihiv regions,” Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
The attack will likely draw further attention to Ukraine’s shortage of air defence missiles.
“While Moscow is investing in ballistic missiles and escalation, such strikes do not always receive the response they should from the world. And as long as Ukraine does not have enough anti-ballistic defence, Russia will not consider peace seriously,” Zelenskyy warned this morning.
Pledging with allies to send more Patriot interceptors to help protect Ukraine, he stressed that “every additional missile saves the lives of our people.”
More drone attack warnings from Kyiv were going live this morning.
Responding to the overnight attacks, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko declared Friday a day of mourning in the city.

ICC separates Taliban probe from US case as Afghan women's fate stays uncertain
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
09:44:05 UTC
18:44:05 KST

ICC judges reportedly ordered prosecutors to open a standalone investigation into Taliban persecution of women, separating it from the probe that also covered alleged US crimes in Afghanistan. Afghan rights advocates warned the split risked undermining comprehensive justice.
Five years after Afghanistan fell into the hands of the Taliban as they captured Kabul, the International Criminal Court has reportedly split its investigation of Taliban crimes from the broader Afghanistan probe in a move that could ease pressure from Washington on the court.
According to Middle East Eye, judges at the ICC's Pre-Trial Chamber II have ordered prosecutors to open a standalone investigation into alleged Taliban persecution of women, separating it from the court's long-running Afghanistan investigation, which also covered alleged crimes by US personnel.
The Chamber reportedly found that Taliban conduct since 2021 is "materially different" from the conduct the original investigation was authorised to examine, and directed prosecutors to open a standalone inquiry.
The ICC's Office of the Prosecutor would neither confirm nor deny the decision to Euronews, but it did indicate that the Taliban are the core concern of its probe.
“The investigation is focused on the Taliban leadership and their alleged crimes of persecuting women and political opponents, including the deprivation of fundamental rights, systematic arrests and torture,” a spokesperson said.
"The Office of the Prosecutor is unable to provide further comment on the investigation, or on the existence or non-existence of any alleged Court filing which is not public," the spokesperson added.
‘Deeply troubling’
Shaharzad Akbar, former head of the Afghanistan Independent Human Rights Commission and now a fellow at Oxford's Wolfson College, did not mince words on the split.
"Any selective justice is deeply troubling," Akbar told Euronews. "It is also alarming to hear the US's bullying, intimidation and attacks on the court are influencing decisions made about investigations."
Akbar said Afghan civil society groups have "repeatedly asked the ICC for comprehensive investigations about all allegations that fall within its mandate," including allegations against US forces, and described Washington's conduct toward the court throughout the investigation as "appalling and shameful”.
The allegations against US personnel in Afghanistan relate primarily to the documented abuse of detainees at CIA detention facilities there, including the Salt Pit black site north of Kabul, and the conduct of US military interrogators.
The US Senate Intelligence Committee's 2014 report on the CIA's detention and interrogation programme found that detainees were subjected to waterboarding, sleep deprivation and other methods that constitute degradation and torture.
The next day, the US Justice Department announced it would not open any new criminal investigations as a result of its findings. It also stated that if any foreign government issued an arrest warrant for a US official in connection with the programme, it would not enforce it.
No US government has ever acknowledged wrongdoing by US military or CIA personnel in Afghanistan.
During US President Donald Trump's first term, the White House applauded an early ICC ruling that declined to open a formal investigation into US personnel’s actions in Afghanistan, calling it "a major international victory" for "patriots”. The decision was later repealed.
Why were the two bundled together to begin with?
Unlike other international tribunals, the ICC does not separate its investigations by belligerents in a conflict. It probes what it calls a "situation” defined by territory and time period.
Afghanistan ratified the Rome Statute in 2003, giving the court jurisdiction over crimes committed on Afghan soil from that date, regardless of who committed them.
When the Appeals Chamber authorised a formal investigation in 2020, it covered the Taliban and its affiliate the Haqqani network, the so-called Islamic State-Khorasan Province group (ISIS-K), Afghan government forces, and US military and CIA personnel, all under a single investigative umbrella.
In 2021, then-prosecutor Karim Khan deprioritised the part of the investigation concerning US conduct, choosing to focus the court’s resources on the Taliban and ISIS-K.
But because the broader Afghanistan “situation” remained formally open, long-standing political pressure from Washington aimed at the investigation as a whole had the potential to affect the case against the Taliban simply because both were part of the same file.
That pressure became even more pronounced ever since Trump returned to office in January 2025, with his administration doling out further sanctions within months against ICC officials tied to the Afghanistan and Palestine investigations.
In December, diplomats told Middle East Eye that at the court's oversight meeting, Washington pressed for both investigations to be dropped entirely as a condition for lifting sanctions on ICC officials.
The July 2025 warrants against Taliban leader Haibatullah Akhundzada and judiciary chief Abdul Hakim Haqqani for the crime against humanity of persecution of women and those perceived as allies of women on political grounds were issued amid those pressures.
Washington to bring down the court?
Last month, the US State Department announced plans for a campaign to “dismantle” the court and "systematically disable" its "ability to operate (and to) target American servicemen or officials, or otherwise threaten American sovereignty."
It said actions could include increased restrictions and visa revocations, as well as travel bans on ICC personnel.
On Tuesday, Washington announced further sanctions on ICC President Tomoko Akane and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, accusing them of "directly" engaging "in efforts by the ICC to investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute officials whose government has not consented to ICC jurisdiction."
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who called the ICC a "corrupt and fatally politicised supranational court," added that it had "maliciously abused its authority and exceeded its mandate.”
The court "repeatedly attempted to assert authority over nationals of the United States and other countries that have not consented to its jurisdiction or ratified the Rome Statute,” according to Rubio.
The US has never ratified the Rome Statute. President Bill Clinton signed it in his final days in office in December 2000, but the administration of George W Bush formally withdrew the signature in May 2002 and notified the UN that the US did not intend to become a party.
US Congress followed that same year with the American Service Members' Protection Act, which authorises the president to use military force to free any US citizen or allied national held by the ICC, legislation informally dubbed the "Hague Invasion Act”.
‘A gift to the Taliban’
Meanwhile, Washington’s actions after pulling out of Afghanistan have gone beyond abandonment, according to Akbar.
"This context has emboldened criminal conduct and extensive violations across the world," she said. "This is a gift to regimes like the Taliban, who can continue with impunity in a context of failing global order and rule of law."
“US’ disregard for international law and its attacks on the court embolden actors like Taliban and feed into their narratives about the Western bias of international tribunals."
Afghanistan under the Taliban has turned into the most repressive country in the world for women, according to a UN assessment in March 2024.
Since August 2021, the Taliban have issued more than 50 decrees systematically removing women from public life in Afghanistan.
Girls are banned from education beyond the sixth grade, making Afghanistan the only country in the world where women are barred from secondary school on the basis of their gender.
Women are prohibited from working in most jobs, including working for NGOs and UN agencies. Parks, gyms and public spaces are also off-limits.
Further edicts were issued with the intent to persecute LGBTQ+ Afghans, empowering "morality police" to punish "moral crimes" and explicitly criminalising same-sex intimacy.
Akbar, who also serves as executive director of Rawadari, an Afghan human rights organisation, said that Afghan women's rights groups, human rights investigators and survivors "have supported the ICC investigation every step of the way and have contributed to the process," while also demanding that the court widens its scope.
What happens now?
None of the Taliban officials under warrant are likely to ever be in custody: the group has complete control over Afghan territory since the US withdrawal in 2021 and has dismissed warrants as “hostility towards Islam”.
Akhundzada has led the Taliban since 2016, when he succeeded Mullah Akhtar Mansour after his death in a US drone strike in Pakistan. Akhundzada has never appeared in public since taking on the role and is believed to operate solely from Kandahar in southern Afghanistan.
He is ultimately responsible for the most restrictive edicts against women.
Chief justice Haqqani has been the main architect of the judicial tools enforcing those edicts, including the return of public floggings and executions.
Asked what the warrants have achieved, Akbar said that although valuable, they have had limited impact.
"We welcomed the news of arrest warrants because it was a moment of justice and accountability after decades of impunity in Afghanistan," she said. "We hoped the warrants would also delay the trend of normalisation of the Taliban."
"To change the situation in Afghanistan we need stronger political will from the region and the Western countries to engage on similar terms with the Taliban and demand reversals on bans and restrictions on the rights and freedoms of women and girls in Afghanistan,” Akbar concluded.

Unexpected twin-city breaks you can take by sleeper train in Europe
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
09:42:56 UTC
18:42:56 KST

Sleeper trains are making it possible to pair destinations with completely different vibes without the airport queues. Here are some unexpected European city pairings connected by overnight rail.
Across Europe, travellers are rediscovering the perks of the sleeper train, with overnight rail services making it possible to link cities that might otherwise feel too far apart for a single trip.
By rail, there’s no need to see each destination as a standalone break. A night train can turn two distant and distinct cities into one itinerary, allowing travellers to leave a European city in the evening and wake up somewhere entirely different the next morning.
Research by Omio, a digital travel booking and comparison platform, found that this mode of travel is gaining pace, with the highest-search sleeper corridors cluster being around Berlin, Amsterdam, Prague, Paris and Sint-Gillis.
According to their analysis of most searched routes by users, travellers are especially curious about these routes:
- Berlin, Germany to Prague, Czechia
- Amsterdam, Netherlands to Berlin, Germany
- Amsterdam, Netherlands to Sint-Gillis, Belgium
- Berlin, Germany to Paris, France
- Amsterdam, Netherlands to Antwerp, Belgium
Overall, Omio also found sleeper train bookings to have steadily increased by 8% year-on-year, with NightJet train bookings up by 15% and 26% up for EuroNight trips.
But where’s the fun in taking the most popular routes? Instead, opt for one of these unexpected European city pairings that you can connect by sleeper train.
Sofia, Bulgaria and Istanbul, Türkiye
From Bulgaria’s capital of open-air book markets, beech-tree forests and the soaring Mount Vitosha, to Türkiye’s city spread across two continents, Sofia and Istanbul offer two very different experiences.
The 10-hour journey aboard the Sofia-Istanbul Express train offers travellers couchette and sleeper accommodations, with a double sleeper ticket costing €15 per person, while a single sleeper costs €35.
To get their hands on a ticket, however, travellers generally have to do it the old fashioned way and buy them in person at the train station in Sofia in Bulgaria, or Istanbul Halkali station in Türkiye.
Berlin, Germany and Budapest, Hungary
Berlin and Budapest may be separated by almost 900 kilometres but a sleeper train makes it possible to link the two capitals in a single trip.
Via the ÖBB Nightjet, travellers can choose from seating carriages, to couchettes or a sleeper cabin. A one-way sleeper cabin ticket from Berlin to Budapest in September starts at €223 per person.
The 12-hour journey from Berlin Hbf to Budapest-Nyugati includes a prepared bed with a pillow and blanket, private washing facilities and breakfast as part of the fare.
Across 16 stops, the overnight train ride calls at stops across cities in Czechia and Slovakia, turning what would have been a short-haul flight into a cross border journey through Central Europe.
Brussels, Belgium and Prague, Czechia
While Brussels is the heart of European politics and policymaking, Prague offers travellers medieval charm, provocative street art and its own miniature version of France's Eiffel Tower – the Petřín Tower (also known as “the Eiffel Tower’s little sister”).
The Belgian capital is connected to this Czech city via the European Sleeper which offers a choice of seats, compact couchette berths and sleeper cabins that can accommodate up to three people with separate beds and seating areas. While their comfort standard sleeper cabin class doesn’t include breakfast, it is included in comfort plus.
A Comfort Standard one-way fare from Bruxelles Midi to Praha hl.n. in September starts at €239.99. The outbound journey from Brussels is around 15 hours and 29 minutes.
Warsaw, Poland and Vienna, Austria
Warsaw and Vienna offer travellers a trip of contrasts: the Polish capital for its its green spaces, including the Łazienki Park that features a lake and strutting peafowl, followed by Vienna’s imperial architecture, grand palaces and castle complexes and historic coffee houses, such as Café Schwarzenberg which has been operating since 1861.
The two destinations are connected by an overnight Nightjet service from Warszawa Centralna to Wien Hbf, cutting across Czechia. The approximately 10-hour-long outbound ride starts at €129.90 in a sleeper cabin in September.
Zurich, Switzerland and Amsterdam, Netherlands
Swap the Swiss Alps for a detour to Amsterdam’s canals with an overnight sleeper connecting Zurich’s lakeside landscapes to the Dutch capital’s museums and famously cycle-friendly streets.
A Nightjet sleeper train from Zürich HB station to Amsterdam Centraal is around a 12 and a half hour ride, with a sleeper cabin starting from €134.90. The journey also calls at stops in Germany, including Bonn and Cologne.

Swiss adapt holiday plans to summer heat
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
09:42:45 UTC
18:42:45 KST

Swiss adapt holiday plans to summer heat
The increasing summer heat is changing the way Swiss people travel. According to a survey, more than half of the population has already adjusted their travel plans because of the heat, or intends to do so in future.
According to a representative survey carried out by Marketagent on behalf of the tour operator Dertour Suisse, 27% of the 1,000 respondents have already adjusted their holiday plans due to the heat. A further 29% intend to do so in future. Meanwhile, 37% do not plan to make any changes.
The shift in travel behaviour is particularly pronounced among younger people: among Generation Z (born between 1995 and 2010), around 65% stated that they had already changed their plans or intended to do so in the future. Among Millennials (born between 1980 and 1995), this figure stood at around 64%. The proportion was significantly lower among Generation X (born 1965–1979) at 47% and among baby boomers (born 1946–1964) at 44%.
More
As heatwaves rise, Swiss climate concerns fall
Despite the hot weather, traditional factors remain the main considerations when choosing a holiday destination. For 47% of those surveyed, good value for money was one of the three most important criteria. This was followed by attractive scenery and natural surroundings at 32%, and peace and quiet, relaxation, beaches and swimming opportunities, each at 31%. Pleasant temperatures were among the most important deciding factors for 21%.
Strategies for coping with the heat vary
Adjusting holiday plans does not necessarily mean travelling north. According to the survey, the most common response to the heat is to opt for different travel periods. Some 38% of those who adjust their plans are increasingly travelling outside the hottest summer months.
Some 31% specifically choose destinations with a cooler climate. A further 28% adapt their activities or the times of day while there.
Holidays in cooler regions, known as “coolcations”, are attracting a great deal of interest. Some 69% of those surveyed considered summer holidays in relatively cool destinations to be attractive. Support was particularly high in the Zurich area, at 76%, and in Graubünden, at 85%.
Booking figures from Dertour Suisse also confirm this trend, as the company announced when the survey was published. Demand for destinations such as Scandinavia, Scotland and Canada has risen by around 21% over the past five years.

• The rebels have used this year's Ebola outbreak to demonstrate their administration in eastern Congo, mounting a response largely separate from authorities in Kinshasa.

• The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Congo has exceeded 5,000, government data showed this week. REUTERS

The family of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, who was killed in an Israeli drone strike in 2024, has slammed the Israeli military's decision not to pursue criminal charges against the IDF personnel who ordered the attack.
Speaking on behalf of the family, Ms Frankcom's brother Mal said the decision to announce the outcome on World Humanitarian Day in particular was "an insult to my sister's memory".
What's next?
The family are continuing to call for an independent judicial assessment of the incident, while Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong says she has no confidence in the IDF's findings.
The statement, issued by Zomi's brother Mal on behalf of the Frankcom family, said family members were "deeply disappointed" by the decision, having spent the past two years waiting for justice while "hoping and calling for an independent criminal investigation".
"Zomi and her colleagues deserve more than an internal, opaque process that ends with a short statement by the Israeli military absolving their soldiers of criminal wrongdoing," they said.
"The families of the victims deserve transparency and an independent judicial assessment of the criminal responsibility for the international humanitarian law violations that took place on that day."
The group was travelling in three armoured cars branded with the World Central Kitchen logo, and driving through part of the Gaza Strip that had been declared a "humanitarian fire control zone" while coordinating movements with the IDF (Israel Defense Forces).
An Israeli drone fired three missiles at the convoy — one at each of the cars in succession — as survivors of the initial strike attempted to move from one vehicle to another.
An Australian investigation into the Israeli government's response to the incident, led by retired defence chief Air Chief Marshal Mark Binskin, found the deaths had been the result of the first vehicle being misidentified due to a number of factors, including the presence of armed security in the vicinity, confirmation bias and a "failure within the IDF to fully disseminate and/or read the detailed movement plan approved by the convoy".
The subsequent strikes were also found to be a breach of IDF procedures and the rules of engagement, echoing the findings of a rapid FFAM ("fact-finding and assessment mechanism") investigation conducted by the IDF in the days following the incident.
Two IDF officers were fired in the weeks after the strikes, while others were reprimanded.
In their statement released on Thursday evening, Ms Frankcom's family expressed disagreement with the finding that there was no wrongdoing involved that merited at least a criminal investigation, highlighting the follow-up strikes as well as the fact that one of the officers involved had reportedly signed a letter earlier that year calling for the flow of aid to Gaza to be restricted.
They also expressed outrage at the timing of the announcement, which came on World Humanitarian Day, an internationally recognised day dedicated to those who have died working for humanitarian causes.
The family had been standing alongside Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong at an event at Parliament House just hours prior to the announcement, launching a humanitarian award in Ms Frankcom's name.
"For it to be announced on World Humanitarian Day, the day the world pauses to remember those who have lost their lives while helping others … is an insult to my sister's memory,"
Ms Frankcom's brother Mal said.
Senator Wong similarly expressed anger at the announcement, saying she had no confidence in the IDF's findings, and calling in Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, to explain the decision.
Calling today's events a "difficult time" in diplomatic relations with Israel, she said she was informed of the IDF's decision just minutes before it was publicly announced, and did not have time to alert Ms Frankcom's family.

====================================================================================================

Blocked ports threaten Ukraine’s economy — reopening seaports seen as vital for survival
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-20
12:38:31 EEST
18:38:31 KST

Volodymyr Shchelkunov, President of the Ukrainian National Committee of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC Ukraine)
Blocked ports mean a blocked economy. Why reopening seaports for all types of cargo is a matter of survival for the Ukrainian economy.
Ukraine has been living and working under the conditions of a full-scale war for the fifth year. Businesses manufacture products under fire, exporters compete on global markets despite destroyed infrastructure, and the state maintains its defense capability to a significant extent thanks to foreign currency revenues generated by the real economy. In this fragile balance, there is one link on which almost everything depends — access to global markets through seaports. Today, that link has been severed.
ince July 2026, the enemy has been systematically attacking civilian vessels and port infrastructure. Ukraine’s deep-water ports have effectively been blocked. Around 90% of the country’s maritime traffic is now at risk. This is no longer a logistics problem affecting individual companies or industries. It is an issue of national macroeconomic stability, the resilience of the hryvnia, and the food security of entire regions of the world.
“Seaports are not just infrastructure. They are the main gateway connecting the Ukrainian economy to the world. When they are closed, it is not one industry that stops — the entire mechanism that generates foreign currency, taxes, and jobs for the country begins to shut down.”
Ports Must Be Reopened for All Types of Cargo
It is important to stress one fundamental point from the outset. The reopening of ports must be full and unconditional — for all types of cargo without exception. Not only for grain, not only for selected “priority” categories, but for the entire range of Ukrainian exports: steel, iron ore, food products, machinery, and construction materials.
The temptation to opt for selective reopening — in the form of a “corridor” for a specific product category — is misguided and dangerous. The Ukrainian economy cannot be divided into “important” and “unimportant” cargoes. The steel and mining sectors generate foreign currency and provide freight volumes for the railway. The agricultural sector feeds the world and brings foreign currency into Ukraine. Rescuing one category while leaving the others under blockade is like saving one lung while the other cannot breathe.
First-Half 2026 Figures: Why Every Export Dollar Is Now Strategic
To understand why the port blockade strikes at the most vulnerable point of the economy, it is enough to look at the official foreign trade statistics for the first half of 2026. They are alarming.
According to the State Customs Service, Ukraine’s total trade turnover in the first half of 2026 reached $70.3 billion: imports amounted to $49.3 billion, while exports were only $21 billion. Goods imports exceeded exports by 2.3 times, or by $28.3 billion. In other words, the country imports almost three times more than it exports.
The trend is even more telling. Compared with the first half of 2025, imports increased by 28% from $38.3 billion, while exports rose by only 5% from $20 billion. The gap is not merely large — it is widening rapidly. Today, exports cover only about 40% of imports.
For the economy, this means one simple and harsh reality: every dollar of export revenue has become a strategic resource. Exporters’ foreign currency earnings help support the hryvnia, pay for critical imports, and reduce pressure on the state’s reserves. The enormous trade deficit is currently being covered by international assistance, and any decision that reduces Ukrainian exports automatically increases that deficit and puts additional pressure on the national currency.
And it is precisely at this moment, when exports are already under severe pressure, that the port blockade is shutting down their main channel. This is a direct blow to the state’s ability to balance its economy.
“We import almost three times more than we export. In such conditions, closed ports are not merely lost logistics — they are a disabled source of foreign currency that the economy critically needs.”
There Is No Real Alternative to the Sea — Only Expensive and Temporary Half-Measures
The most dangerous illusion in the current situation is the assumption that everything will be fine because cargoes can simply be “rerouted” through Danube ports or by rail to EU ports. On paper, this may look logical. In practice, it does not work as a full replacement and can only serve as a partial, temporary solution. There are specific and measurable reasons for this.
Danube ports are not deep-water ports. Their throughput capacity is limited. They can absorb only up to an additional 30% of maritime cargoes, and only for exports to nearby markets. Long-distance destinations — China, East Asia, North Africa — are physically inaccessible through the Danube.
EU ports are not deep enough. Large ocean-going vessels require depths of around 19 meters, which Odesa can provide. Neighboring EU ports offer depths of only up to 15 meters. This is not a bureaucratic restriction but a physical one: a large vessel with a deep draft simply cannot enter a shallow port. This is why entire continental markets can be reached only through Ukraine’s deep-water ports.
Western border crossings are already overloaded. Their throughput capacity is limited, while logistics through them are two to three times more expensive. The need to replace Ukrainian railcars with European ones and the much longer logistics route make such transportation economically unviable for entire categories of cargo.
This is where a second, man-made problem emerges. The government’s decision to raise freight rail tariffs by 30% starting in August 2026 came at the worst possible moment, coinciding with the port blockade. Instead of reducing the cost of alternative logistics and supporting exporters, the state made those routes even more expensive. Fully replacing maritime exports with land routes would require government compensation of up to $100 per tonne — a level that makes such substitution simply unrealistic.
“Alternative routes are not a bridge to the other side — they are a narrow and unstable crossing. A few can get through, but not the entire economy. Only the reopening of deep-water ports can restore logistics and access to global markets.”
Steelmaking Is on the Verge of Shutdown, While Global Food Security Is Under Threat
The mining and metals sector — one of the country’s largest export industries — is suffering the most severe impact from the port blockade. Steelmaking is uniquely dependent on logistics at every stage. Every additional dollar in transport costs multiplies across the production chain. This is why the combination of the port blockade and higher railway tariffs has dealt the industry a double blow. Logistics costs for iron ore have doubled, while for pig iron they have increased two to three times. In many cases, additional transport costs now exceed the profit per tonne of product. This means export contracts become loss-making, while plants already operating under constant attacks are pushed to the brink of shutdown.
In recent weeks, we have already seen the enemy strike enterprises in the mining and metals sector. But the shutdown of a steel plant is not only a loss of exports. It means thousands of jobs in single-industry cities, reduced railway freight volumes, and the collapse of entire supplier chains. This is why steel and iron ore cannot be left “outside the brackets” when ports are reopened.
For the agricultural sector, the consequences of the blockade extend far beyond Ukraine. Our country is one of the world’s largest food suppliers. Ukraine accounts for around 6% of global wheat exports, 12% of corn exports, and more than one-third of global sunflower oil trade. When the maritime corridor is blocked, these volumes disappear from the global market — and food prices rise.
Therefore, reopening Ukrainian ports is not only a Ukrainian issue. It is an element of global food security and the stability of EU markets.
The Cost of Inaction: What One Year of Closed Ports Could Mean
To keep the discussion concrete, the cost must be stated directly. If the maritime corridor is not restored, Ukraine risks losing more than 10% of GDP over the course of one year. Pressure on the hryvnia would increase as export revenues could fall by an estimated $17 billion. The state budget could lose around $8.5 billion in tax revenues. More than 30 million tonnes of agricultural products might fail to reach global markets.
This is not a pessimistic scenario for dramatic effect. It is the logical consequence of shutting down the channel through which the majority of Ukrainian exports move. And it is important to recognize a simple relationship: Ukraine is currently financially dependent on support from its partners, and destabilizing the Ukrainian economy increases the burden on Europe rather than reducing it. Open Ukrainian ports are in the interest not only of Kyiv, but also of Brussels and Washington.
“Closed ports do not save money — they destroy it. Every month of blockade means less foreign currency revenue, fewer taxes, fewer jobs, and more pressure on the hryvnia.”
What Needs to Be Done
The situation requires not declarations but specific, coordinated decisions by the Ukrainian government with the support of international partners. The priorities are clear.
The primary and irreplaceable task is to restore safe navigation and reopen Ukraine’s deep-water ports for all types of cargo without exception. Without this step, all other measures will remain half-measures.
At the same time, while the blockade continues, the state should ease rather than increase the burden on alternative logistics. The recent 30% increase in freight rail tariffs works against exporters and against the state itself under current conditions. It should be reversed in order to stimulate, rather than hinder, transportation through western border crossings.
Supporting the transit of Ukrainian goods through EU ports as part of joint initiatives with partners would also be logical. In addition, given that the EU imports a significant share of steel products, work should be carried out toward reallocating EU steel import quotas in favor of Ukraine — at a level no lower than Ukraine’s actual exports to the EU in 2025.
